rubric.evidence: The page separates current ChromeStatus evidence (milestone listing Enabled by default at 151; feature detail desktop+Android 151, status Proposed, updated 2026-06-16; historical origin-trial stage at 146) from source maturity. WICG/nav-speculation PR #426 is open and unmerged, its spec preview is proposal text, and the explainer is non-normative. Parent review corrected two proposal-boundary errors: console warnings are optional ('may'), and the explainer's list-rule intent is not visibly enforced by the open PR diff, which parses the member generically and propagates it through the predicate/document-rule candidate path. The discrepancy is documented rather than resolved by invention.

Feature id 5074313831120896 appears in the v151 authoritative milestone inventory. The stable route and ChromeStatus identity match. Listing status and feature-detail status are displayed separately; the page does not turn the detail's Proposed text into a shipment contradiction or erase the listing evidence.

Seven h2 sections cover at-a-glance metadata, syntax and parser behavior, motivation, examples, interim compatibility, specifications/proposal status, and related sources. The page covers boolean/default behavior, prefetch rejection, optional warning, intended list-rule use and open-PR discrepancy, eligibility/CSP motivation, developer-triggered timing, no direct feature detection, and activation preconditions.

The page explains the distinction between preparing a prerender as a form submission and triggering speculation. It no longer promises activation: creation, retention, eligibility, navigation type, and URL matching are explicit conditions. The simple GET example now derives the candidate URL from current form data and replaces the prior rule script rather than accumulating stale candidates.

The companion snippet is safe, bounded, and labelled as a simple GET-form composition; debounce is explicitly an omitted application helper. Parent MCP review discovered that the embedded Showcase syntax builder generated fabricated top-level form_submission JSON. The upstream demo was repaired and pushed as chrome-platform-showcase commit 56dbab3f: it now emits {prerender:[{urls,eagerness,form_submission:true}]} and omits the member when unchecked. Both states were exercised at 390px.

The banner says 'Not Baseline-tracked · Chrome-only evidence' rather than assigning an unsupported Baseline status. MDN and BCD contain no form_submission entry as of 2026-07-25. Chrome desktop+Android 151 evidence, Edge not-separately-reported, and Firefox/Safari No signal are distinct. The page states that no direct client-side API can detect this JSON member and recommends progressive enhancement plus real activation validation.

Primary links cover ChromeStatus, Chromium runtime feature inventory, open PR #426 and its spec preview, the WICG explainer, issue #322, Chromium issue 346555939, BCD script.json, and the chrome.dev GET-form demo. External links use rel=noopener. Showcase route identity matches the same ChromeStatus feature.

Single main and h1; sequential h1→h2 structure; four semantic tables with captions and scoped headers; descriptive lazy iframe title; banner role=note with accessible label. The upstream embedded builder's h1→h3 skip was corrected to h1→h2 in commit 56dbab3f, and its checkbox has a visible programmatic label.

At 390×844 parent MCP measured document scrollWidth=390, all four tables 342px client/scroll width, no page overflow, and readable word-boundary wrapping. The live iframe loaded after scroll, generated JSON without post-interaction overflow, and the upstream builder remained contained at 390px. Desktop and mobile support remain ok/ok in responsive-support.json.

The iframe uses this feature's stable Showcase syntax-builder route and same ChromeStatus id. Parent did not repoint the embed when a defect was found; it repaired the published demo in place under its durable compatibility contract (56dbab3f). The existing Showcase root conformance suite covers adjacent speculation prerequisites, not direct form_submission acceptance, so this review does not present it as native field proof.

openQuestions: PR #426 remains open and unmerged. Its current diff propagates form_submission through the predicate/document-rule path even though the explainer says form-submission speculation is restricted to list rules. Re-check this discrepancy when the PR changes or merges; do not encode list-only parser rejection as settled until the proposal text does.
